title: Orchestrator surge fallback and action catalog (post-incident)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident investigation and action catalog for a dedicated-capacity throughput shortfall that manifested as degraded tail latency and per-pool throughput reduction during a multi-customer synthetic surge. This ticket captures timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and prioritized long-term fixes for the orchestrator and autoscaler subsystems.
impact_summary: During the surge window (2025-11-05 10:12–10:42 UTC) multiple Dedicated pools experienced sustained throughput drops of 20–60% and 99th-percentile latency spikes up to 4x for affected tenants. Several customers reported degraded availability to the Redwood API and activated on-call escalation. No data loss; primary impact was request throttling and increased error rates for large inference jobs.
timeline: 10:10 UTC - synthetic load generator ramps; 10:12 UTC - orchestrator begins rebalancing; 10:16 UTC - autoscaler decisions oscillate and queue lengths increase; 10:21 UTC - first alerts for per-pool throughput drop; 10:25 UTC - automated fallback to smaller-quantized model variant triggered but hit capacity fragmentation; 10:30 UTC - manual failover to regional spare pools begins; 10:42 UTC - stabilized after headroom reallocation and temporary throttles; 11:15 UTC - full traffic normalization confirmed.
root_cause_summary: A recent scheduler heuristic change (scheduler v2.3.7) switched certain placement scoring to a 'least-connections weighted by recent completions' metric. Under bursty arrival patterns this produced shard hotness: a small subset of GPU nodes received disproportionate allocation. Concurrently, autoscaler rollback logic misinterpreted pending pod counts as available headroom due to a race when Kubernetes API moved pods from Pending to Terminating, causing the autoscaler to under-provision. The combination produced sustained queue backpressure and triggered fallbacks that fragmented capacity and reduced effective throughput.
investigation_notes:
- Collected kube-scheduler logs, orchestrator allocation traces, and autoscaler decision history.
- Reproduced allocation skew in testbed by replaying the exact arrival distribution using the synthetic surge harness.
- Discovered autoscaler metric 'available_capacity_estimate' was reading an in-flux gauge that exposed a race between pending->terminating transitions.
- No hardware faults found; degradation purely software/orchestration-related.
short_term_mitigations: Rollback scheduler heuristic to stable v2.3.6 in production (hotfix deployed 10:40 UTC)
Apply autoscaler patch to ignore pods in Transition states when computing headroom (deployed 10:38 UTC)
Enable emergency regional redistribution policy to move new allocations to underutilized spare pools (activated 10:28 UTC)
Throttle large-batch customer lanes temporarily and prioritize low-latency interactive traffic (activated 10:27 UTC)
Deploy a temporary circuit breaker that rejects new long-running jobs when pool queue length exceeds threshold (activated 10:29 UTC)
long_term_actions: Design and land a deterministic placement simulator in CI to detect placement skew regressions before rollout
Add 'pending->terminating' state class to autoscaler headroom calculation and unit tests for state transitions
Instrument per-shard allocation fairness metrics and expose them in the Console with anomaly alerts
Implement per-customer queue shaping and weighted fair-queueing to limit noisy neighbor amplification
Introduce autoscaler hysteresis tuned for bursty arrival patterns and add synthetic-burst load tests to perf suite
Ship a graceful rollback capability for scheduler heuristic toggles with canary traffic shard isolation
Update runbooks: include a step to validate available_capacity_estimate with kube-apiserver snapshot before autoscaler decisions
followups: ENG-663322 (create placement simulator and CI integration)
ENG-663324 (console: allocation fairness dashboard and alerts)
PM-4450 (communicate incident summary and mitigation to impacted customers and Sales)
DES-307 (Console UX: surface emergency redistribution controls and explanations)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scheduler rollback proves stable for 72 hours with no allocation skew; 2) Autoscaler headroom calculation has new unit+integration tests covering transition states; 3) Placement simulator merged and running in main CI; 4) Console shows per-shard fairness metrics and at least one alert configured; 5) Customer communication sent and postmortem published.
risk_and_open_questions: 1) How will per-customer shaping interact with Dedicated SLA guarantees for high-commit tenants? 2) Are there GC/cleanup windows where pending->terminating races are more frequent (e.g., during rolling kernel upgrades)? 3) Need to quantify cost impact of adding spare reserve pools vs. long-term autoscaler tuning.
next_steps:
- Merge autoscaler state-machine patch and run full integration suite (owner: Marco Chen)
- Begin placement-simulator spike (owner: Elena Rodriguez)
- Draft customer-facing incident summary and run by legal/comm (owner: Aisha Patel)
notes: This incident highlights cross-cutting risk between small scheduler heuristics and autoscaler state assumptions. Priorities: prevent placement hotness regressions with pre-rollout simulation, and make headroom computation conservative and observable. We'll schedule a cross-team retro with infra, serving-runtime, and product next week.
